A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTSyn by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial scientific revisions.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices E–G report original synthesis benchmarks, ablations, cross-domain utility results and conditional-classification experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original few-shot synthesis benchmarks, reconstruction ablations, metadata robustness tests and text/date-time reconstruction results.

M1.justification: Section 3 replaces the contrastive, magnitude-aware aggregator and separately trained type-specific decoders with a variational autoencoder and schema-guided decoder. Numerical embeddings change from a learned number autoencoder to repeated quantiles; categorical reconstruction uses cosine-softmax probabilities and cross-entropy. A transformer replaces the residual-MLP diffusion backbone, with conditioning expanded to column names. Fine-tuning now updates the decoder as well as diffusion. Appendix F adds text/date-time components.

E1.justification: Across both main texts and appendices, four benchmarks remain: Obesity, Liver, Abalone and Shoppers. NPHA, Diabetes, Sick and Churn disappear, while seven benchmarks including Faults, HTRU2 and Insurance are added. v2 introduces broad OpenTab pre-training, eBay/NFL text/date-time reconstruction and unseen/permuted/renamed-column scenarios. v1's conditional-classification and column-augmentation evaluations disappear. Regression and cross-domain evaluation already existed in v1 Appendix F.

E2.justification: The evaluated synthesis comparator set drops CTABGANPlus and AutoDiff and adds SMOTE, TVAE and TabSyn, as verified in the benchmark tables. CTGAN, TabDDPM, AIM, PATE-CTGAN and GReaT remain. v2 Table 5 additionally evaluates an adapted pre-trained TabSyn alongside its non-pre-trained version; TabSyn was only discussed as related work in v1.

E3.justification: v1 uses 70/5/25 pre-training/fine-tuning/test splits and half-feature downstream tasks. v2 reports separate OpenTab pre-training, 80/20 downstream splits, 30–500-shot subsets and fixed 500-row synthetic samples. Training budgets and fine-tuning controls change. Precision/recall and authenticity are introduced, while DCR and Wasserstein/JS reporting disappear; regression utility changes from adjusted R-squared to RMSE. GReaT's reported initialization also changes from randomized to pre-trained distilgpt2.

E4.justification: v1's Diabetes decoder/pre-training ablation is replaced by metadata and column-name ablations under in-distribution, unseen-column and permuted-column conditions, plus a three-model pre-training comparison. v2 adds uninformative-header robustness tests and Insurance latent-space visualizations in Appendices H–I. The synthesis-diversity case study changes from Obesity to Indian Liver Patient. These analyses address substantially different questions about transfer and schema dependence.

E5.justification: v1 specifies ten fine-tuning/test splits using seeds 0–9 and defines reported spreads as standard deviations. v2 describes three generation trials per subset with a common holdout, without specifying seeds. Parenthetical spreads remain in fidelity/privacy tables but are not defined, and utility Figure 2 and Tables 8–9 omit uncertainty. Both the variability assessed and the coverage of uncertainty reporting change substantially.

E6.justification: Most result entries are replaced under changed models, datasets and protocols, including removal of v1's conditional-generation, column-augmentation and conditional-classification results. v2 Table 8 reports classification F1 of 0.83 versus real-data 0.82 at 100 shots, but 0.84 versus 0.88 at 500 shots. New reconstruction and robustness results appear in Tables 4, 10 and 11. These are newly reported findings, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The formal model definitions in Section 3 are substantially replaced. v1's deterministic row representation, magnitude-aware objective and supervised contrastive decoding give way to Gaussian variational latents, KL-regularized reconstruction and a revised schema-conditioned denoising objective. These are substantive mathematical changes rather than notation edits. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 removes the broad abstract/conclusion claim of uniquely and consistently improving utility beyond real training data, emphasizing benefits in low-data regimes. Contributions are redefined around a cross-table autoencoder, schema-conditioned diffusion transformer and large-scale pre-training. The conclusion's novelty claim changes from the first consistent utility boost over real data to the first integration of large-scale pre-training into tabular generation through latent diffusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of column names acting as metadata proxies and positional encoding failing under column permutation. It acknowledges diminishing benefits as downstream data grows and conjectures limitations in the transfer-learning setup. Pre-training interpretations now include negative transfer for GReaT and TabSyn. Appendix A adds the difficulty of obtaining semantically meaningful category names, while retaining earlier bias and pre-training privacy caveats.

D1.justification: v2 documents revised architecture and optimization settings, OpenTab filtering and file inventories, baseline pre-training adaptations, and the GPT-4o metadata-generation model, prompt and example. Hardware changes from one A10G GPU to four, and Appendix J adds comparative pre-training runtimes. v1's fine-tuning runtime and code-release disclosure are omitted. The metadata procedure is newly documented; v1 did not establish how its metadata was produced.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and central comparison with non-transferable tabular generators largely remain. Focused additions include beta-VAE, sample-level synthetic-data auditing, BART and low-data augmentation references; CLIP and gradient-surgery references disappear. Novelty is refocused on large-scale latent-diffusion pre-training. The CT-BERT citation's updated title/publication is a bibliographic update, not a newly introduced work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, methodology, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 changes from five subsections to three, incorporating implementation into the model description. Appendices are substantially reorganized, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. Citation style changes from numbered references to author–year.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn for the revised architecture. Wide per-dataset result tables are replaced by compact aggregate summaries and utility-versus-shot plots. The synthesis t-SNE figure is rebuilt for another dataset, and a latent-space visualization is added. New appendix tables display pre-training inventories, reconstruction, robustness and computation results. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is stronger evidence for cross-table generalization: v1 pre-trained on other rows of its evaluation datasets, whereas v2 reports a separate OpenTab corpus, evaluates unseen downstream tables across data budgets, and directly tests metadata dependence and schema robustness. Narrowing the utility claim to low-data regimes better reflects the findings. Fewer trials, missing utility uncertainty and aggregation across datasets reduce auditability, but the revised experimental design substantially strengthens support for the paper's central foundation-model claim.
